title:
Real images.
Built by AI.
Fixed by you.
say: In part two, an A.I. builds a deck from a real microscopy image, and then we fix the model's mistakes in the mask editor, step by step.

title: Ask your AI for a deck
say: Here's the prompt. I gave Claude, with the Hooman skill, a real image of human nuclei, and the mask from a simple threshold model. It cut the image into tiles where the model made mistakes, drew the model's outlines, checked the deck against the app's rules, and handed me a zip file.

title: Import the zip
say: On the phone, tap Import deck, and pick the zip. Each card is one tile of the image, with the model's outlines in red.

title: Spot the mistakes
say: Look closely. Some small nuclei have no outline at all, and on the left, several nuclei are stuck together as one object. That needs fixing, so swipe up.

title: Start from the model
say: Start from model copies the model's outlines into the editor. Every object gets its own number and colour, so you only fix what's wrong.

title: Cut merged nuclei apart
say: Choose Cut, and draw a line across the narrow neck between two nuclei. The object splits in two, and each part keeps its own number.

title: Add the missed nuclei
say: Now the missed nuclei. Choose the wand, and tap each one. It fills the bright area in a single tap. The slider makes the last fill smaller or bigger.

title: Touch up by hand
say: For fine work, the brush paints the selected object and never spills into a neighbour, and the eraser removes pixels. Undo and redo cover every step.

title: Save, then export
say: Save, and the corrected mask is stored with your answer. Export the answers, and the zip holds every mask, and which objects came from the model and what you changed.

title: Back to your AI
say: Give the export back to the A.I. It reads your corrected masks, counts what you fixed, and has them ready as training data for a better model.

say: In part three: tracking cells over time, reviewing your answers, and making the answer buttons your own.
